highlight.title: MCP 2026-07-28 Release Candidate Delivers Stateless Production-Ready Protocol
highlight.summary: <cite index='4-1,4-5'>The headline change is that MCP is now stateless at the protocol layer</cite>, completing a major revision that addresses enterprise scalability concerns. <cite index='4-12'>This release gives MCP the foundation we expect it to grow on for a long time: a protocol that runs statelessly on commodity HTTP infrastructure, an extensions framework where capabilities like Tasks and MCP Apps can ship on their own timeline</cite>.

resources.title: Red Hat Announces MCP Server for RHEL Developer Preview
resources.why_now: <cite index='6-2,6-3'>Red Hat is announcing the developer preview of a new Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for Enterprise Linux (RHEL). This new MCP server is designed to bridge the gap between RHEL and Large Language Models (LLMs), enabling a new era of smarter troubleshooting</cite>, showing MCP's enterprise traction.

resources.title: The 2026 MCP Roadmap: Enterprise Readiness and Transport Scalability
resources.why_now: <cite index='1-20'>Enterprises are deploying MCP and running into a predictable set of problems: audit trails, SSO-integrated auth, gateway behavior, and configuration portability</cite>. <cite index='1-6'>It now runs in production at companies large and small, powers agent workflows</cite>, requiring mature governance structures.

resources.title: AI Tooling for Software Engineers in 2026: Agent Adoption Reaches 55%
resources.why_now: <cite index='11-1,11-3'>AI agent usage rising: 55% of respondents now regularly use AI agents, with staff+ engineers leading adoption on 63.5% usage</cite>. <cite index='11-17,11-18'>Claude Code has gone from zero to be the #1 tool in only eight months. Released in May 2025, it's already the most-used AI coding tool</cite>, indicating rapid tooling shifts.

resources.title: Developer AI Tooling in 2026: Terminal-Native and Agent-First Workflows
resources.why_now: <cite index='12-21,12-22'>There's a quiet renaissance happening at the command line. Tools like Claude Code, GitHub Copilot CLI, and Codex CLI are bringing AI directly into the developer's most powerful interface: the terminal</cite>. <cite index='12-6,12-8'>The best AI developer tools in 2026 are the ones that fit into how developers already think and work, rather than asking developers to conform to how AI works. MCP respects the fact that context lives in existing tools</cite>.

claude_take: <cite index='16-11,16-12'>In 2024, the industry was dominated by copilots: tools that draft, suggest, and assist. In 2026, the standard is shifting to agents: tools that research, act, and iterate without step-by-step human direction</cite>. MCP's evolution toward stateless, production-ready infrastructure positions it as the connective tissue for multi-agent systems, while the explosive growth in terminal-native AI tooling suggests developers are demanding workflow integration over flashy interfaces. The next 6 months will likely see MCP become the de facto standard for agent interoperability as enterprises demand governance and reliability at scale.
